label: Morocco Atlas + Sahara
summary: 7 nights from Marrakech over the High Atlas to the Erg Chebbi dunes (Christmas Eve in a desert camp), then north to the Middle Atlas cedar forest for Barbary macaques. Fly out from Casablanca via Cairo and land in Nairobi at about 04:55 on Dec 28.
verdict: Worth it if you want a big change of scenery and culture before Kenya: Atlas passes, kasbahs, gorges, Sahara dunes and the macaques. The wildlife is thin next to East Africa, though: apart from the macaques and camels it is mostly birds. The main drawbacks are the long Dec 27 flight day via Cairo, with no nonstop to Nairobi, and desert nights near freezing. It adds about $2,000 pp all-in over the base trip. Checked: Level 2 advisory (Sep 4 2026), visa-free entry, the AT251 Sun/Tue/Fri pattern and MS848 (daily, 13:30-20:25) are all confirmed. Changed: flagged that MS849's Cairo departure has moved between 20:55 and 23:55 during 2026 (the 20:55 slot would break the connection), corrected the Azrou-CMN distance to ~300 km, and confirmed that the budget sums (~$3,495 pp, +$1,995 vs base) and every low ≤ planned ≤ high range hold.

safety.advisory_level: US State Dept Level 2: Exercise Increased Caution (terrorism). Advisory reissued Sep 4 2026, level unchanged.
safety.summary: Morocco is one of the more stable and tourist-friendly countries in Africa. The Level 2 rating reflects a general terrorism risk; terrorists may target tourist sites, transport hubs and markets. The last deadly attacks on tourists were the 2011 Marrakech cafe bombing and the 2018 killing of two hikers near Imlil. The everyday risks are petty theft, medina hustlers, and mountain driving in winter. Merzouga is close to the closed Algerian border, but the tourist dune area is routinely visited and safe.
precautions: Hire a licensed driver and drive in daylight only; the Tizi n'Tichka pass (2,260 m) and the Midelt road can get snow or ice in late December. Check road status the night before.
In the Marrakech medina, ignore 'the square is closed' and 'follow me' faux guides; agree prices before henna or photos at Jemaa el-Fna, and watch for pickpockets in crowds.
Do not wander east of the Erg Chebbi tourist zone toward the Algerian border, and stay with your camp guide at night.
Drink bottled or filtered water and go easy on raw salads for the first days; carry rehydration salts.
Pack for cold: desert camps and Azrou can drop below 0 C at night. Bring a warm layer, a hat, and a sleeping-bag liner.
Women may get verbal attention in medinas; modest dress helps, and firm 'la, shukran' (no thanks) works.
Stay airside at Cairo (CAI) on the EgyptAir transit, and keep the whole routing on one ticket so a missed connection is the airline's problem. EgyptAir punctuality is mediocre (~50-60% on time).
Enroll in STEP; carry a copy of your passport, since there are police checkpoints on rural roads.

visa: US passport: Morocco is visa-free for up to 90 days (passport must be valid 6+ months on entry; one blank page). Paris (CDG) airside transit needs no visa, and the EU EES/ETIAS systems do not apply to airside transit. Cairo transit: no Egyptian visa needed if you stay airside. Kenya eTA is still required as in the base plan, so make sure it covers a Dec 28 entry.
weather_dec: Dry season, mostly sunny. Marrakech highs ~18-20 C, lows ~5-7 C. Ouarzazate/Dades: highs ~16-18 C, nights ~0-3 C. Merzouga/Erg Chebbi: days ~17-20 C, nights ~1-5 C (camps provide heavy blankets). Azrou/Ifrane (1,250-1,650 m): highs ~10 C, nights below freezing; snow is possible, and the macaques in snow are a bonus. Tizi n'Tichka can close briefly after snowfall. Short days: sunset ~17:45.
highlights: Christmas Eve in an Erg Chebbi dune camp: camel trek at sunset, stars, Berber drumming, sunrise from the 150 m dunes
Barbary macaques in the Cedre Gouraud cedar forest near Azrou (the only macaque in Africa, endangered)
Crossing the High Atlas on the Tizi n'Tichka pass to the UNESCO ksar of Ait Benhaddou
Todra Gorge (300 m walls) and the Dades Valley 'road of a thousand kasbahs'
Marrakech medina, Jemaa el-Fna night market, Jardin Majorelle and Berber Museum
Desert birding around Merzouga/Dayet Srji (desert sparrow, fulvous babbler, maybe flamingos if the lake has water)
Gnawa music village of Khamlia on Christmas Day
drawbacks: Weak on 'exotic wildlife' compared with Kenya: the macaques are the only real mammal highlight; fennec fox and Barbary sheep sightings are rare

Getting to Nairobi is awkward: there is no confirmed nonstop from Morocco. The best timing is EgyptAir MS848 CMN 13:30 to CAI 20:25, then MS849 to NBO. MS849 has shown both 23:55 and 20:55 Cairo departures in 2026; only the 23:55 slot connects, so verify the December timetable before booking
Dec 26 (~5h road) and Dec 27 (~3.5h road + ~13h of flights and layover) are back-to-back hard days; the Dec 28 Nairobi rest day absorbs it

Outbound Dec 19 is a Saturday, and the Royal Air Maroc LAX-CMN nonstop (AT251, 10:20 departure) only flies Sun/Tue/Fri, so you connect via Europe. The exception is leaving a day early, Fri Dec 18. Turkish via Istanbul forces an overnight in Istanbul and loses a Morocco day
Cold nights in the desert and the Middle Atlas; some budget riads and auberges have weak heating
Late December is peak European holiday season in Marrakech and Merzouga: book camps and riads now
Upgrade option: a luxury desert camp ($180-350 pp/night) and a private 4x4 with a guide add ~$400-700 pp
Cheaper option: shared 3-day Marrakech-Merzouga-Fes tours (~$190-300 pp), but they involve 9-10h drive days, which breaks the pace rule

legs.detail: Overnight transatlantic, e.g. Air France/Delta LAX-CDG afternoon departure, arriving ~10:00-11:30 Dec 20. Alternatives: Iberia via MAD, or a Star Alliance ticket via FRA/MUC. Royal Air Maroc's LAX-CMN nonstop AT251 does not fly Saturdays (Sun/Tue/Fri only).
Paris-Marrakech (Air France/Transavia/Royal Air Maroc), ~2-3h connection; arrive RAK late afternoon. Then ~25 min taxi or riad pickup to the medina (~150-200 MAD).
Private driver over the High Atlas via the Tizi n'Tichka pass (2,260 m). ~190 km; stops at an argan co-op and pass viewpoints, lunch at Telouet optional.
Via Ouarzazate, Skoura palmery, the Dades Valley and its gorge switchbacks to Todra Gorge. ~280 km with frequent stops.
Tinghir-Alnif-Rissani-Merzouga, ~200 km. Drop luggage at the auberge and keep a small overnight bag.
Camel trek (or 4x4 if preferred) into the Erg Chebbi dunes at sunset to the camp.
Camel or 4x4 back after the dune sunrise; rest of day easy in Merzouga.
Erfoud-Errachidia-Ziz Gorges-Midelt-Azrou, ~370 km. Break at Errachidia and lunch in Midelt; arrive at the Cedre Gouraud forest by ~15:00 for macaques. This is the longest drive, at the 5h limit.

Leave ~07:30 via Meknes on the A2/A1 toll motorways to Casablanca Mohammed V airport (~300 km), arriving ~11:00 for the 13:30 departure. Backup: Fes airport (1h15) plus a Royal Air Maroc domestic flight to CMN.
EgyptAir MS848 CMN 13:30 (T2) to CAI 20:25 (T3), A321neo, operates daily per 2026 tracker data. ~3.5h airside connection.

EgyptAir MS849 CAI 23:55 Dec 27 to NBO 04:55 Dec 28 (737-800). Some 2026 dates show a 20:55 departure instead, which would not connect, so verify the December schedule before booking. Backups: Qatar QR1396 CMN 20:50 Dec 26 to DOH 06:00, then QR1341 DOH 18:45 to NBO 23:50 Dec 27 (needs a Dec 26 Casablanca departure and drops Azrou). Or Turkish TK618 CMN Dec 26 to IST with an overnight, then TK607 IST 18:45 Dec 27 to NBO 01:25 Dec 28.

itinerary.title: Depart LAX
itinerary.details: Afternoon flight LAX-CDG (~10.5h, overnight). Sleep on the plane.

itinerary.title: Arrive Marrakech
itinerary.details: Land CDG ~10-11:30, connect to RAK (~3.5h), arrive late afternoon. Riad pickup (~25 min). Mint tea, early night. Travel ~6h today plus yesterday's 10.5h.

itinerary.title: Rest + medina
itinerary.details: No transport. Slow morning. Jardin Majorelle + Berber Museum, souks, Ben Youssef Medersa. Sunset from a cafe terrace over Jemaa el-Fna, food stalls at night. Meet the driver for a briefing.

itinerary.title: Over the Atlas
itinerary.details: Driver 08:30. Tizi n'Tichka pass, ~4h road with stops. Afternoon walk through the Ait Benhaddou ksar, climb to the granary at sunset. Moussier's redstart on the pass.
itinerary.meals: B, L roadside tagine, D guesthouse (half board)

itinerary.title: Valley of kasbahs
itinerary.details: ~4h road: Ouarzazate, Skoura palmery, Dades Gorge switchbacks, Todra. Late-afternoon walk into the Todra Gorge (300 m walls).

itinerary.title: Christmas Eve in the dunes
itinerary.details: Morning gorge walk, then ~3h road to Merzouga. ~15:30 camel trek 1-1.5h to the camp, sunset on the dunes, dinner, drums, stars. Cold night (1-5 C).

itinerary.title: Christmas rest day
itinerary.details: Dune sunrise, camel back ~1h, then breakfast and a shower at the auberge. Lazy day. Optional: Khamlia Gnawa music, Dayet Srji lake birding (desert sparrow, flamingos if wet), afternoon nap.

itinerary.title: Cedars + macaques
itinerary.details: Depart 08:00. ~5h road: Ziz Gorges, Midelt (lunch), Azrou. ~15:00 Cedre Gouraud forest for the Barbary macaques; Levaillant's woodpecker possible. Snow possible.

itinerary.title: Long haul to Kenya
itinerary.details: Leave 07:30, ~3.5h (~300 km) to CMN airport. EgyptAir MS848 13:30 to CAI 20:25 (~5h), ~3.5h airside wait, MS849 23:55 to NBO, landing 04:55 Dec 28, then straight to the Nairobi rest day.

lodging.name: Riad Dar Najat (or similar budget medina riad)
lodging.why: Walkable to the square and souks; a quiet courtyard for jet-lag recovery
lodging.alternatives: Riad Laaroussa or Riad Yasmine (~$90-150 pp, more style); Equity Point hostel (~$20 pp)

lodging.name: Kasbah guesthouse, e.g. Dar Mouna
lodging.why: Wake up to the ksar at sunrise without a long drive

lodging.name: Gorge auberge, e.g. Hotel Yasmina or Auberge Le Festival
lodging.location: Inside or near the Todra Gorge
lodging.why: Lets you walk the gorge in the late afternoon and early morning

lodging.name: Standard Erg Chebbi desert camp (private tent with bed)
lodging.location: Erg Chebbi dunes, ~1h camel from Merzouga
lodging.includes: Camel trek both ways, dinner, breakfast, blankets; sometimes shared bathroom
lodging.why: The Christmas Eve highlight; standard camps are fine, so pick one with en-suite or heated tents

lodging.name: Merzouga auberge, e.g. Kasbah Mohayut or Riad Madu
lodging.location: Merzouga village, at the dune edge
lodging.style: Auberge with pool and dune views
lodging.why: Christmas rest day with hot showers after the camp; luggage stays here
lodging.alternatives: Ali & Sara's Desert Palace and similar

lodging.name: Azrou/Ifrane hotel, e.g. Hotel Le Panorama Azrou
lodging.location: Azrou town, 15 min from the Cedre Gouraud
lodging.why: Close to the macaque forest and on the motorway route to Casablanca

budget.item: Full multi-city ticket: LAX-RAK Dec 19 (via Paris/Europe), CMN-CAI-NBO Dec 27 (EgyptAir MS848/MS849), NBO-LAX Jan 16 (TK608/TK9)
budget.notes: Replaces the $1,500 base; delta ~+$900 pp (range +$500 to +$1,400). Components: one-way Morocco-NBO fares seen at ~$630-710; festive LAX-Morocco one-way ~$800-1,100; NBO-LAX one-way ~$800-1,100. A single Star Alliance ticket (LH/TK to Morocco + EgyptAir + TK home) gives connection protection. Estimate only; no live festive fare was confirmed, so verify.

budget.item: 7 nights: 2 riad, 1 kasbah, 1 auberge, 1 desert camp, 1 auberge, 1 Azrou hotel (double rooms shared)
budget.notes: Sum of the lodging list: 70+35+30+75+35+30. Most stays half board. The high end adds a luxury camp and nicer riads.

budget.item: Private driver + car, 6 days Marrakech to Casablanca airport (one-way) + RAK airport transfer
budget.notes: ~$150-180/day per vehicle incl. fuel and driver lodging, plus a one-way surcharge, split by 2. Get quotes from local operators; packaged 4-day private Marrakech-Fes desert tours list at ~$750-940 pp including lodging. Shared tours are ~$190-300 pp but have 9-10h days.

budget.item: Majorelle + Berber Museum, Ben Youssef, Ait Benhaddou, gorge guide, Khamlia music, tips (driver, camel guide)
budget.notes: Majorelle + Berber Museum ~200 MAD combined; tip the driver ~$10-15/day per car.
Tagine lunches ~$6-12; half board covers most dinners.

budget.item: Morocco visa-free; Egypt airside transit no visa
budget.notes: Kenya eTA is already in the base plan.

budget.item: Local SIM/eSIM, warm layers, laundry, buffer
budget.notes: Total ~$3,495 pp all-in vs the $1,500 base, so ~+$1,995 pp.

wildlife.name: Barbary macaque
wildlife.odds: Very high (~90%); habituated troops near the road

wildlife.name: Desert sparrow
wildlife.where: Merzouga area (birding guides know the spots)

wildlife.name: Greater flamingo
wildlife.odds: Low-moderate; depends on the lake having water after rain

wildlife.name: Fennec fox
wildlife.odds: Low (~10%); tracks are common, sightings are not

booking.task: Price and book the multi-city ticket (LAX-RAK Dec 19 / CMN-NBO Dec 27 / NBO-LAX Jan 16). Confirm that the December MS849 departure is 23:55, not 20:55, so the connection from MS848 (arr 20:25) is legal; prefer one ticket. Compare with the Qatar and Turkish backup routings.
Book the Erg Chebbi camp for Dec 24 and the Marrakech riad: peak European holiday period.
Book a licensed private driver for Dec 22-27 (one-way Marrakech to Casablanca airport); confirm the 07:30 Dec 27 departure and the motorway route.
Book the Ait Benhaddou, Todra, Merzouga and Azrou guesthouses (half board).
Travel insurance with trip-delay cover (two long connections); check that the Kenya eTA covers Dec 28 arrival.
Reconfirm all flight times (EgyptAir has shifted MS849 several times in 2026); pack warm layers.
Brief the driver; check the Tizi n'Tichka snow status for Dec 22.

fatigue: Travel hours per day. Dec 19: ~10.5h flight. Dec 20: ~6h (connection + 3.5h flight + transfer). Dec 21: 0 (rest). Dec 22: ~4h road. Dec 23: ~4h road. Dec 24: ~3h road + 1.5h camel. Dec 25: ~1h (rest). Dec 26: ~5h road. Dec 27: ~3.5h road + ~5h flight + ~3.5h layover + ~5h overnight flight (arrives NBO 04:55 Dec 28). Dec 28: Nairobi rest day (Kenya plan). Pace: the ~5h max road rule is met every day, with Dec 26 at the limit. There is a rest day after the long-haul arrival (Dec 21) and after the desert (Dec 25). The weak point is Dec 26-27: two hard days back to back, ending in an overnight flight. The Dec 28 Nairobi rest day softens it. If that is too much, drop Azrou and the macaques and fly Errachidia-Casablanca on Dec 26, or overnight in Casablanca.
safety_short: Stable and tourist-friendly. Risks: general terrorism alert, petty theft, medina hustlers, winter mountain roads.
